question: Article 25a of the Visa Code requires the Commission to annually assess the level of cooperation by third countries in relation to readmission. The Commission consistently chooses to use incentives to improve such cooperation, but shies away from using a more punitive approach towards third countries that have a poor track record of facilitating the return of their nationals staying illegally in Member States. As regards the Commission’s assessment for 2023 in accordance with Article 25a: 1.
How many countries were assessed in 2023? Did one or more of these countries receive a positive assessment regarding their cooperation in connection with returns that year? If so, which?

What were the most common problems preventing returns to these countries? Is the Commission considering other concrete steps to improve cooperation on return and readmission, for example by making effective cooperation a precondition for development aid?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (24.1.2025) Ensuring cooperation from third countries on readmission is a priority for the EU. To this end, relevant policies, tools and instruments of the EU and Member States should be pulled together in a strategic way, with a tailor-made approach.

Under Article 25a of the Visa Code1, the Commission has proposed visa measures towards six third countries due to insufficient cooperation on readmission. The Commission proposal for a revised General System of Preferences (GSP Regulation)2 includes a withdrawal criterion related to cooperation on readmission of own nationals.

Talent partnerships with third countries can enhance legal pathways while supporting broader strategic engagement on migration management. The Commission is not able to answer the other questions raised by the Honourable Member, as the answers are part of the Report from the Commission to the Council on the assessment of third countries’ level of cooperation on readmission in 20233 adopted on 20 July 2024.
